description: Soy Geordano, desarrollador web de Lima. Construyo FireSync: un mapa y calendario que unifica los focos de calor de los satélites MODIS y VIIRS (NASA FIRMS) para ver, sin duplicados, dónde y cuándo hay fuego. Uso PHP, MySQL, JavaScript y Leaflet. Busco: analista de datos o GIS (Python/QGIS), diseñador UX/UI y alguien que arme la presentación de 3 minutos. Si te interesan los incendios, los datos satelitales o el impacto ambiental, únete: avanzamos rápido y con plan.
summary: FireSync is a web app that turns 25+ years of NASA satellite fire detections into a monthly fire calendar and early warnings for every region of Peru. It answers the challenge by harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS hotspots into one consistent series: VIIRS S-NPP is the reference, NOAA-20 detections are scaled with a cross-sensor factor, and MODIS years before VIIRS (2001–2011) are converted with a log-log model fitted on the overlapping years, all on a common grid. With that series, FireSync compares the current month against each region’s normal and flags when fire is coming worse than usual, together with clear actions. Alerts reach people where they are: WhatsApp messages, printable bulletins and radio-ready text. This matters because in 2024 wildfires killed 35 people in Peru, and most fires start as agricultural burns that get out of control. A farmer warned before burning can prevent one. The method works anywhere NASA FIRMS has data; Peru is our pilot.
details:
What it does
FireSync turns NASA satellite fire detections into a simple answer for each region of Peru: is fire this month coming worse than normal, and what should we do? It shows a fire calendar (which months are the high-risk season in each region), compares the current month and recent periods against the historical normal (median and typical range), and highlights anomalies such as “+344% – well above normal”. An interactive map shows recent hotspots over NASA GIBS satellite imagery, a department-level choropleth of anomalies, and lets users click a department or draw any area to get its own calendar and trend.

How it works – harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS
MODIS (1 km, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m, since 2012) detect fire differently, so their raw counts cannot be compared directly. FireSync builds one consistent series:

  1. Detections are downloaded from the NASA FIRMS API and archive, then de-duplicated into daily cells on a fine grid, so one fire is not counted several times.
  2. VIIRS S-NPP is the reference sensor. NOAA-20 detections are scaled with a cross-sensor factor estimated from days when both satellites observed the same cells.
  3. For the years before VIIRS (2001–2011), MODIS counts are converted to VIIRS-equivalent values with a log-log model fitted on the overlapping years.
  4. The harmonized counts are aggregated on a 0.1° monthly grid and masked with the real polygons of Peru’s 25 departments, so each region only counts its own fires.
    A “Method” section in the app explains each step for specialists, step by step.

Benefits and target users

  • Farmers and rural communities: know before burning whether this is a dangerous month.
  • Municipalities, civil defense and fire brigades: plan patrols, campaigns and resources ahead of the season.
  • Specialists and researchers: download harmonized CSV data and review the method.
  • Information reaches people where they are: a one-tap WhatsApp message, a printable one-page bulletin with anomalies and recommended actions, and short radio-ready text, in Spanish and English.

Expected impact
In 2024 wildfires killed 35 people in Peru, and most fires start as agricultural burns that get out of control. Early, local and easy-to-understand warnings can prevent fires before they start, rather than only reporting them once they are burning. The method relies only on open NASA data, so it can be replicated in any country covered by FIRMS.

Tools and technologies

  • Backend: PHP 8.1 with PDO, MySQL, and scheduled cron jobs on cPanel hosting for automatic data updates.
  • Frontend: a vanilla JavaScript single-page app, HTML and CSS, and Leaflet 1.9.4 with canvas rendering.
  • NASA data: FIRMS (MODIS, VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20), GIBS imagery (VIIRS True Color, Black Marble) and EONET events.
  • Other data: Peru department boundaries (GeoJSON) and NOAA CPC ENSO context.

What makes it creative

  • It turns a technical problem, harmonizing two sensors, into a “fire calendar” anyone can read.
  • It answers “is this month worse than normal for my area?” instead of only showing dots on a map.
  • It closes the last mile with WhatsApp, paper and radio, because many rural users have no internet or dashboards.
  • It offers two levels in one product: a simple view for communities, and a specialist area with perspective, method and data export.

What our team considered

  • Scientific honesty: transparent methods, sensor differences explained, and data sources shown on every view.
  • Accessibility: plain language, a mobile-first design, a printable format, and a guide by user role.
  • Low connectivity: lightweight pages and cached results.
  • Security and privacy: API keys kept on the server, and protected configuration files.
  • Scalability: the same pipeline works for any region or country that NASA FIRMS covers.
